1.title: Exam Orientation and How to Study
1.text: Welcome to Module zero: Exam Orientation and How to Study. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. The exam at a glance. The four question styles. The seven categories and their weight. How to answer every question. A four-week study plan. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: Exam overview, syllabus map and answer technique (all categories). Exam format: forty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; twenty-six correct answers (sixty-five percent) pass. Validated against: the official eye til Foundation (Version five) syllabus, version five point zero (February two thousand twenty-six).

1.title: The exam at a glance
1.text: The exam at a glance. Questions. forty, all multiple choice, one mark each. Time. sixty minutes (seventy-five if the exam is not in your native or working language). Pass mark. twenty-six of forty (sixty-five percent). Negative marking. None, so always answer. Book. Closed book. Thinking level. Bloom level one and two: recall and understanding. Level. Foundation; it is the entry point to the higher eye til (Version five) qualifications. Exam tip: The exam tests definitions and understanding, not hands-on skill. If you can say what a term means and tell it apart from a similar term, you pass. eye til four Foundation was the earlier exam. Version five replaced it, so use Version five names: eye til Value System, eye til Product and Service Lifecycle (eight activities), digital product and service management.

1.title: The four question styles
1.text: The four question styles. Standard. What you see: A stem and four options. Tip: Find the keyword in the stem first. Negative. What you see: The stem says not or E X C E P T. Tip: Rare; rewrite it as "three are true, find the false one". Missing word(s). What you see: A sentence with; pick the word(s). Tip: Read the sentence aloud with each option.

1.title: The four question styles, continued
1.text: The four question styles. List. What you see: Four numbered statements; pick the option naming the two correct ones. Tip: Judge each statement true or false, then match the pair. List questions are never negative: exactly two statements are correct.

1.title: The seven categories and their weight
1.text: The seven categories and their weight. one. Category: Key eye til terms and definitions. Weight: thirty percent. Marks: twelve. two. Category: The four dimensions of product and service management. Weight: ten percent. Marks: four. three. Category: The eye til Product and Service Lifecycle. Weight: ten percent. Marks: four. four. Category: The eye til Value System (principles, governance, value chain, practices, improvement). Weight: forty percent. Marks: sixteen. five. Category: Value stream identification, mapping and management. Weight: five percent. Marks: two. six. Category: eye til and A I. Weight: two point five percent. Marks: one. seven. Category: eye til and other frameworks (dev ops, prince two). Weight: two point five percent. Marks: one.

1.title: The seven categories and their weight, continued
1.text: The seven categories and their weight. The figure shows this: Syllabus map: seven categories and where each module fits. Exam tip: Categories one and four are seventy percent of the marks. Spend most of your study time on key terms and on the eye til Value System.

1.title: How to answer every question
1.text: How to answer every question. Read the last line of the stem and find the keyword. Name the term in your head before you look at the options. Eliminate options that describe a different term. Choose the option that matches the definition, not the one that merely sounds modern or helpful. Never leave a blank; there is no penalty. Common traps: output versus outcome, utility versus warranty, customer versus user versus sponsor, problem versus error versus known error, continuous delivery versus continuous deployment.

1.title: A four-week study plan
1.text: A four-week study plan. one. Modules: one to four. Goal: Key terms, value, dimensions. two. Modules: five to seven. Goal: The eight lifecycle activities. three. Modules: eight to eleven. Goal: Value System, principles, practices, improvement. four. Modules: twelve to fifteen. Goal: Value streams, A I, other frameworks, mock questions. Re-read the Quick Reference Card at the end of each module, and do the Exam Q and A the next day.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Northwind Bank asks how many questions it must answer correctly to pass the eye til Foundation (Version five) exam. Which answer is right? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: twenty-six of forty. The pass mark is twenty-six of forty, which is sixty-five percent.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A candidate is unsure about a question and has thirty seconds left. What should the candidate do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Answer it, because there is no negative marking so a guess costs nothing. There is no negative marking, so an answer can only help.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. In a List question, which statement is true? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Exactly two statements are correct. List questions have two correct statements, and they are never negative.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which two categories together carry seventy percent of the marks? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Key terms and definitions, and the eye til Value System. Key terms (thirty percent) and the Value System (forty percent) together make seventy percent.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How long is the exam, and what is the extra time for a non-native language? Answer: sixty minutes; seventy-five minutes in total (twenty-five percent extra). Question two. What Bloom levels does the exam use? Answer: Level one (recall) and level two (understanding). Question three. Name the four question styles. Answer: Standard, Negative, Missing word(s) and List.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which category has the highest weight? Answer: The eye til Value System, at forty percent. Question five. Is the exam open book? Answer: No, it is closed book. Question six. What replaced eye til four Foundation? Answer: eye til Foundation (Version five).

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Format: forty questions, sixty minutes, twenty-six to pass, no negative marking, closed book. Styles: Standard, Negative (rare), Missing word(s), List (two correct). Weights: thirty or ten or ten or forty or five or two point five or two point five percent. Method: Keyword, name the term, eliminate, choose the definition. Never: leave a question blank.
